title: Finding the trombone and the idea of playing melody
summary: He tried the church choir leader's trombone, got lessons from his school orchestra leader, and decided the trombone should play melodies like a cello rather than tailgate style.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Picking up the horn: first instrument and the trombone

blocks.x: Now, as I said before, my father being a minister, we were continually shifting around and different things, and the choir leader of our church was a trombone player, and he used to use his trombone only on Sunday, and so it stayed up in the vestibule of the church. And I keep -- kept noticing this horn laying there, and, now, being interested in music, I wondered what kind of sound this was. And I finally got nerve enough up to open it and try to make a note.

Now, since I had been playing tuba, the lip positions are very similar, and so I could make a note or a few notes, and the orchestra leader of our orchestra in school was a pretty good teacher at most any instrument, and so I applied to him for some lessons, which he granted, and so he taught me my first lessons on playing the trombone.
Well, the trombone at that time was more or less a tailgate instrument, you know, that the slur and -- a tailgate type of thing. And --
Did that interest you at that time?

--the -- no, I wasn't interested in tailgate. I by this time had had enough music and enough acquaintance with most all of the instruments, and I happened to remember that the trombone was about the same tonal level as the cello, and the cello was the violin, just a large violin in the lower registers. So the trombone, having nothing but a slide, I thought of the trombone as the violin of brass instruments, and then I began to wonder why couldn't the trombone play the same type of music as the cello, and I couldn't see why it had to still resort to that tailgate business.

So I began to try to play melodies, using the melodic type of playing instead of the tailgate type, which I enjoyed quite a bit. I liked to play melodies, and I'd had enough all-around, we'll say,music, so I would practice airs and different songs, different things like that on the trombone, and still it seemed that nobody was doing this very much, at least out on the coast.
Do you remember about how old you were when you were trying these things on the trombone?
